title: Proceedings under Section 4 of Community Disputes Resolution Act 2015 for Cases of Smoking Near Balconies or Windows in Homes
what_it_is: Proceedings under Section 4 of Community Disputes Resolution Act 2015 for Cases of Smoking Near Balconies or Windows in Homes

sections.label: CDRA smoking claims evidence
sections.summary: Claims for second-hand smoke can be brought under section 4 of the CDRA, requiring evidence of unreasonable interference.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Member will therefore be aware that claims can be brought under section 4 of the Community Disputes Resolution Act 2015 (CDRA) for cases of smoking near balconies or windows in homes when the second-hand smoke interferes with a neighbour's enjoyment of his or her property.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Section 4(1) of the CDRA states that a resident must not, by an act or omission, cause unreasonable interference with another neighbour's enjoyment or use of place of residence.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Section 4(2)(a) states that the interference may include an act of causing excessive smell and smoke.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: As a Court of Law, the CDRT requires a claimant to present sufficient evidence to show that the respondent caused excessive smoke and smell to such an extent that it causes unreasonable interference.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Some examples include letters or contemporaneous messages which are exchanged between the neighbours which may point to or suggest the source of the second-hand smoke, written records that set out the specific dates and times of the acts in question and also show an established pattern of smoking, and if possible, photographs or video-recordings which capture the particular resident in the act of smoking.

sections.label: CDMF review and complaints
sections.summary: An inter-agency committee led by MCCY is reviewing the CDMF, and over 2,400 people sought help for second-hand smoke.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: As separately conveyed to this House, an inter-agency committee led by MCCY is reviewing the CDMF and is studying a range of proposals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the last two months, over 2,400 people in Singapore have approached me for help with regard to them being affected by second-hand smoke in their homes.

sections.label: CDMF review considers mediation
sections.summary: The CDMF review committee is considering measures including mandating mediation in some cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And that is why the CDMF review committee is looking at measures, which I have explained in the prior written answer to this House.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We are considering a range of options, including in some cases, mandating the mediation.
